title: [Feature] Fix guided decoding blocking bitmask memcpy (#12563)

experiments.name: guided_decode_bitmask_async_copy
experiments.workload: Single-request generation with xgrammar guided decoding, Llama 3.1 8B on one H100; decode-phase tok/s with the token-bitmask H2D copy blocking vs async.
experiments.note: Diff is a one-liner in xgrammar_decoding.py: self.token_bitmask.to(scores.device) -> .to(scores.device, non_blocking=True), letting the CPU pre-launch sampler kernels instead of blocking on cudaStreamSynchronize. Numbers are the author's single-request H100 benchmark posted in a comment (87.5 tok/s unoptimized, 92 tok/s optimized).

reported.scope: end-to-end single-request decode throughput (tok/s) for Llama 3.1 8B on H100 with xgrammar guided decoding
reported.scale_short: Author's number is full E2E single-request decode tok/s on an H100; the win is a GPU async-copy / kernel-pre-launch effect not reproducible on CPU. TO MAKE 1:1: run Llama 3.1 8B with xgrammar guided decoding single-request on a CUDA device and measure decode tok/s with the bitmask copy blocking vs non_blocking=True.
reported.scale_note: The speedup comes from hiding a blocking H2D bitmask transfer behind sampler-kernel launches (nsys traces in the PR body). It only manifests under real CUDA stream overlap; an isolated CPU timing of the .to() call cannot exercise the stream-synchronize that the fix elides, so the ~5% E2E figure is not 1:1 with any CPU microbench.

environment: reported-only: author's published GPU numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
